name: Rokeim
overview: Rokeim is a male figure mentioned uniquely as the father of Hananiah in Rahlfs' Septuaginta version of Nehemiah 3:8. His name does not appear in the traditional Hebrew Masoretic Text (BHS), highlighting a textual variant in the biblical manuscripts. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are provided in the scriptural record.
namesAndTitles: The only recorded name for this individual is 'Rokeim,' which is presented as a proper name without any given meaning or divine origin. This name appears solely in the Greek Septuagint text and does not carry an explicit meaning in the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Rokeim only as the father of Hananiah, with no other relationships or familial connections mentioned. Beyond this paternal link, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Rokeim's significance lies primarily in the textual tradition of the Septuagint, where he is identified as the father of Hananiah, a contributor to the rebuilding efforts described in Nehemiah 3:8. His presence in this version but absence in the Hebrew text underscores the importance of manuscript variations in biblical studies. Although a minor figure, Rokeim serves to connect the community involved in the restoration of Jerusalem's walls, reflecting the collaborative spirit of the post-exilic period.
